references.text: Jacob used cunning to deceive his father Isaac, just as the Gibeonites used cunning (בְּעָרְמָה) to deceive the Israelites.
Jacob's sons answered Shechem and Hamor with deceit (בְּמִרְמָה), a similar theme of deception as in the actions of the Gibeonites.
The law that whoever kills by cunning shall be taken from the altar and put to death shows the seriousness of deceptive behavior in Israel.
Proverbs speaks of the wise who cover shame, but the shrewd (עָרוּם) acts with knowledge, sharing the same root as the word for cunning in Joshua 9:4.
The simple believe everything, but the shrewd (עָרוּם) considers their steps, showing a contrast to the deceptive actions of the Gibeonites.
The continuation of the Gibeonites' deception, where they show old bread and worn-out wine skins as proof of their claimed long journey.
Jesus encourages his disciples to be wise as serpents and innocent as doves, a positive use of shrewdness in contrast to the Gibeonites' deceit.
